meta.edit_contract: AI CONTRIBUTORS READ THIS: the shared source of truth is the GitHub repo Torres0990/devildriver-bible (public) — read devildriver.json there, not a cached copy. The unit of change is a NOTE. To ADD knowledge (a new Style, a new mechanic, a new zone): append an object to notes with a unique kebab-case id, a category from the categories list (or add a new category object — build.py generates its page automatically), status locked|decided|open, and an updated date. To EDIT: modify the note in place and bump updated. NEVER change the meaning of a locked note without Sebastian's explicit approval — locked means he confirmed it final. Style kits live in category styles, one note per Style, using the style-kit schema in the style-system note. Bodies use plain text: blank line = new paragraph, lines starting with '- ' = bullets. If you have repo write access, commit directly; otherwise hand the new/edited note JSON to Sebastian and he will route it. After editing: python3 build.py, then python3 deploy.py.
meta.how_to_use: Notes are the unit of knowledge. AI consumers: read the edit_contract above before adding or changing anything; read prompting note for prompt composition. Humans: the HTML pages render the same notes readably.
meta.name: DevilDriver Design Bible (notes)
meta.status_convention: locked = Sebastian confirmed, final. decided = current direction, can revisit. open = undecided, Sebastian decides.

notes.body: Each team owns an enormous demon. The demons duel each other in the central city while the players skirmish around them — fighting enemy players, attacking the enemy demon, and gathering souls to buff their own demon. An unbuffed duel always ends in mutual destruction; souls are the tiebreaker that lets one demon live.
notes.title: Pitch

notes.body:
- Demons are the match clock — everything orbits their duel
- Souls are the only progression inside a match
- No builds, no loadouts — a Style is a complete fixed kit
- Big health pools — nobody gets deleted instantly
- Verticality everywhere — wall-running, climbing, three stacked zones
notes.title: Design pillars

notes.body:
1. Skirmish — teams fight over positioning and the first souls while the demons open their duel.
2. Demon duel — the demons fight in the main city, driven toward mutual kill unless soul buffs tip it.
3. Demon fall — one demon dies. Its team permanently loses respawns.
4. The hunt — the surviving demon hunts the remaining enemy players alongside its team. Match ends on team wipe.

Win condition: wipe the enemy team after their demon falls.
Respawns: while your demon stands, dead teammates respawn after a delay (delay length: open). When your demon falls, no more respawns.
notes.title: Match flow

notes.body:
Two arms, as designed. Standard humanoid rig, cheap to animate. No hidden limb gimmicks - keep it simple. Hands are OPEN, not fists (design correction 2026-10-05).

Kit pivot 2026-10-05: BRAWLER, not swordsman. No katana. Fights with punches and kicks; throws fireballs from the chest core. Legendary finisher: cuts the enemy demon in half (method open).

crystal.note: Separate small asset so it can pulse with demon health / ult timer

notes.title: Samurai demon (brawler)

notes.body:
Serious, threatening, unmistakably airborne flying leviathan. Celeste / light-blue body with white-cyan glow accents. Buildings float weightlessly around it so gravity control reads instantly in the silhouette. Not cute, not cartoonish — must read as a rival boss to the samurai.

Kit: manipulates gravity around BUILDINGS only — never directly on players (fairness rule, locked). Makes structures float or ignore gravity temporarily; terrain changes are neutral opportunities for both teams. Asymmetric kit, equal match effectiveness vs the samurai — no soul advantage means the duel still ties. Special abilities, timed ultimate, anti-rider responses, telegraphs and counters.

notes.title: Gravity leviathan

notes.body:
- Boss body: 30K tris (samurai demon carries no weapon - brawler kit)
- Per demon: ~30K tris; both demons: ~60K tris (well under 15% of a mid-range mobile frame budget (~750K-1M tris/frame))
- Chest crystal separate for health/ult pulsing and as fireball origin
- Draw calls (materials per model) matter more than polygons; transparency overdraw is the silent killer
- Player Style weapons (dual katana) need their own budget - open

notes.body: No character selection, no weapon mixing, no skill trees, no builds. A Style is a complete fixed kit: manifested equipment, attacks, defense, movement, abilities. Start with one Style; later additions are complete new Styles.
notes.title: Player model: Style

notes.body:
- Strong parry
- Wall-running and heavy vertical movement
- Demon climbing — players can climb demons and attack body regions
- Structure damage only via specific Style abilities, never basic attacks
- Large health pools — no instant deletions
notes.title: Core mechanics

notes.body:
Tiebreaker for the demon duel. Feeding souls to your demon is the only way it survives the mutual-kill outcome.

Cadence: one soul every 90 seconds. No bank or deposit system.

Open: sequential limited souls vs unlimited recurring spawns vs one rotating active soul; delivery method; whether souls drop on player death; buff magnitude per soul; spawn location rotation.
notes.title: Souls

notes.body:
- One for all (outnumbered): buff activates when one player fights two or more enemies with teammates absent.
- Last person standing: temporary comeback window for the final player — activates only after they have taken enough damage. Not instant, not permanent, not a second life.

Numbers, cooldowns, visuals, and interaction with demon death: open.
notes.title: Comeback systems

notes.body:
A Style is a complete fixed kit — picking it is the entire pre-match decision. Schema for a Style note:

- name: the Style's name
- fantasy: one-line combat fantasy (e.g. 'untouchable duelist who turns defense into offense')
- equipment: manifested gear (weapons are part of the kit, not separate picks)
- attacks: basic attack behavior
- defense: parry/block/dodge identity within the strong-parry system
- movement: how it wall-runs, climbs, repositions — what makes its traversal distinct
- abilities: named abilities, including which one damages structures
- vs-demons: how this Style fights or supports around the demons
- status: open until Sebastian locks it

notes.title: Energy pool
notes.body:
Max Energy: 100 points, shared across all mobility actions.

- Dodge: 30-35 points per dash — about 3 consecutive dodges before empty.
- Sprint: ~5 points per second.
- Full recharge: 3.0 seconds (0 to 100%).
- Energy regenerates while walking — no forced standing idle during neutral play.

notes.title: Dual Katana (Fire/Void)
notes.body:
The starter Style — every new player picks this kit free at creation. Working title; proper name open.

Fantasy: untouchable duelist who shreds defense with Void, then executes with Fire.

Equipment: two manifested katanas — Katana F (Fire) and Katana V (Void). Weapons are part of the kit, not separate picks.

Attacks: real-time stance swapping between the two katanas. Katana V is the neutral opener — gap closing, crowd control, defense shred. Katana F is the payoff — high raw damage plus Burn DoT stacks once the target's defense is open.

Stance swap rules: 1.0 second rapid swap window immediately after each transition for fluid combo extensions; 7.0 second swap lockdown once the window expires — no infinite stance spam.

Defense: Katana V utility plus the universal strong-parry system.

Movement: energy-based dodges and sprint (see energy pool); wall-running per core mechanics.

Abilities: Burn DoT — Fire strikes stack burn damage over time, constant health pressure. Defense Shred — Void strikes strip armor/resistance, applying a vulnerability debuff.

Vs demons: open — not yet specified how this Style fights around the demons.

notes.title: Monetization pillars
notes.body:
Core pillar: zero pay-to-win. No weapon or item bought with real currency ever grants a numerical stat advantage.

Cosmetics and skins are pure aesthetic — character, weapons, visual effects — with 0% stat boost.

notes.title: Style unlocks
notes.body:
Every new player picks 1 base Style free at creation.

Additional Styles unlock two ways: in-game playtime/currency earned from matches and challenges, or direct premium purchase (pay-to-skip — the kit is fixed, so no stat advantage).

New Styles launch with a temporary paid Early Access window before becoming earnable in-game.

notes.title: Base attributes
notes.body:
Base values every Style is tuned against: 2,500 HP, 100 ATK.

Open question: whether HP stays flat across Styles or varies per Style - see the style-stat-variance note.

notes.title: Energy pool (mobility)
notes.body:
Max Energy: 100 points, shared across all mobility actions.

- Dodge: 30-35 points per dash (~3 consecutive dodges max)
- Sprint: ~5 points per second
- Full recharge: 3.0 seconds (0 to 100%)
- Energy regenerates while walking — no need to stand idle during neutral play.

notes.title: Dual katana stance kit (proposed starter Style)
notes.body:
The primary starter weapon kit: real-time stance swapping between two elementally distinct katanas. Recorded as a Style — one fixed kit, no weapon mixing.

Katana F (Fire) — Offense & Execution: high raw damage and Burn DoT stacks (non-lethal and lethal) ticking over time; the damage payoff stance once defense is opened.

Katana V (Void) — Defense Shred & Utility: hits strip armor/resistance (vulnerability debuff); crowd control and gap closing; the neutral opener. Once shredded, swap to Katana F to maximize output.

Stance swap rules: see base-attributes note (1.0s rapid window, 7.0s lockdown).

Stance Swap Rules (kit-specific, not universal):
- Rapid Swap Window: 1.0 second immediately following a stance transition, allowing fluid combo extensions.
- Swap Lockdown Cooldown: 7.0 seconds after the rapid swap window expires, preventing infinite stance spamming.

Intentional swap mechanic (decided 2026-10-06): swapping stances does NOT auto-fire an ability. The swap ability only triggers if the outgoing katana's passive is stacked (e.g. at least 1 Burn stack while on Fire) - then the incoming katana throws its ability. Swapping without stacks fires nothing; instead it grants a small movement-speed buff. Purpose: swapping for positioning or combo setup never punishes the player with an unwanted ability lock (swap -> stuck in animation -> deleted). Open: whether the swap consumes the stacks (recommendation: yes, so cashing in is a real decision). Empty-swap speed buff: Sebastian proposed 30% for 3s - feedback (David): too hot, it becomes a strategy (free mobility vs dodge costing 30-35 energy) and undercuts the intentional-swap design. Recommendation: 10-15% for 2-3s, or 30% as a ~1s burst.

Ability slots (Sebastian, 2026-10-08). Buttons are stance-contextual: each slot does the Fire version in Fire stance, the Void version in Void stance.

Slot 1:
- Fire: puts the katana on fire — attack speed increases; each hit on an enemy charges a Burn stack.
- Void: gap-closer slash that gets close to the locked enemy.

Slot 2: SWAP. The swap-triggered abilities (under the intentional swap rule above):
- Void → Fire: down-to-up slash that throws the enemy up (launcher) — a quick slash to combo.
- Fire → Void: throws a ranged slash that paralyzes the enemy on contact for 0.8 seconds; leaves them frozen even if mid-air.

Slot 3:
- Fire: puncture mobility skill — if it hits an enemy, the enemy is sent flying; airtime is physics-based, same as the Void → Fire launcher (no fixed duration).
- Void: 6 quick slashes, a close-range attack (Sebastian's wording also said "does 3 quick attacks" — 6 vs 3 unclarified, open).

CC philosophy (Sebastian, 2026-10-08): the paralyze and airborne are combo extenders, not hard stuns — they exist to keep the combo going. Durations stay as short as possible while still long enough to continue a combo; the 0.8s paralyze figure is a starting point, not locked; launch and knockback airtime are physics-based, not fixed durations.

notes.title: Armor modules (CONFLICT — needs Sebastian's call)
notes.body:
Proposal: exactly 1 Active Armor Module equipped per match. Modules are consumable — wear down and expire after a set number of matches (currency sink).

- Vitality Core: flat max-HP bonus beyond 2,500 + slow continuous regen (active).
- Purifier Node: instantly cleanses all debuffs (hard counter to Burn stacks / Defense Shred).

CONFLICTS WITH LOCKED PILLARS: (1) 'No builds, no loadouts' — picking 1 module per match is a loadout choice. (2) 'No persistence / no economy between matches' — consumables expiring across matches implies cross-match persistence. Resolve: drop modules, fold them into Styles as fixed kit parts, or revise the pillars.

notes.title: Monetization model
notes.body:
Core pillar: ZERO pay-to-win. No weapon, module, or item bought with real currency ever grants a numerical stat advantage.

- Cosmetics & skins: pure aesthetic, 0% stat boost (character, weapon, VFX skins)
- Pay-to-skip: grind vs direct buy for Style unlocks; paid Early Access passes for new Styles

notes.title: Style progression
notes.body: Every new player selects 1 base Style free. Additional Styles unlock via in-game playtime/currency (matches + challenges) or direct premium purchase (pay-to-skip, no stat advantage). New Styles launch with a temporary paid Early Access window, then become grindable.

notes.title: Currency sinks
notes.body:
- Consumable armor modules (if the module system is approved — currently open/conflicted)
- Cosmetics: character, weapon stance, and visual effect skins

notes.title: Per-Style stat variance (open question)
notes.body:
Question from Sebastian (2026-10-06): should base health stay flat at 2,500 for all Styles, or vary per Style?

Recommendation: vary it. With no builds, the Style IS the build - flat stats waste the main differentiation axis. But keep 2,500 HP / 100 ATK as the anchor and express every Style's stats as deltas with a paired cost (e.g. +500 HP means -mobility, -energy, or -offense). Rules:
- Sidegrades only, never strict upgrades - a tankier Style must give something up.
- Because Styles are unlockable (grind or pay), an unlocked Style must never read as pay-to-win; every delta must be visible in the kit with its tradeoff.
- List each Style's deltas in its kit note so matchups stay readable.

notes.title: Onboarding: first-session flow
notes.body:
First session: tap from feed, pick 1 free starter Style (one tap, big visuals, ~5 seconds - no menu maze), straight into a bot match. Skip-tutorial button always available.

No separate tutorial. Contextual coaching inside the bot match, triggered by situation not by timer:
- Running near a wall: 'You are running close to a wall! Double jump to run on it!'
- Enemy guarding: 'Enemy is guarding! Hold attack for a heavy attack!'
- Dodge prompt tied to joystick direction: 'Press dodge, you will dodge to where your wheel is pointing.'

The bot match has two jobs: teach the hands AND sell the fantasy. Bots let the player land the cool stuff - first heavy breaks a guard, first soul buffs their demon, they watch their giant demon smash something.

Mindlessly easy by design: no option overload, straight to fun. Teach Styles and how to check abilities - nothing else until the player is retained.

Ability check UI: tap the Styles button -> see all Styles (locked ones visible as the shop window) -> tap your Style -> tap any ability to inspect it. Suggestion (David, not locked): inspect shows the move performed as a short clip, not just text.

notes.title: Match intro: demon descent
notes.body: No ground spawns. All players start standing on their team's demon. The demons descend into the main city together and the players wall-run down nearby buildings into the fight. This is the opening spectacle of every match. Intro is ~10 seconds, no skip needed. Reference pose: player character standing triumphant atop the demon during descent (see assets/refs/descent-hero-pose.jpg) — this is the poster's hero shot.

notes.title: Respawns: sky drop
notes.body: While your demon stands, dead teammates respawn after a delay (delay length: open). Respawns drop from the sky in a protected no-fall-damage state, landing back into the fight. The drop is STEERABLE — players choose their landing spot, turning respawn into a small tactical decision (wall-run straight back in on landing near buildings).

notes.title: Adaptive metal soundtrack
notes.body:
Metal soundtrack with adaptive intensity layers, mapped to the locked match flow:
- Skirmish: sparse and tense (clean guitars, heartbeat drums) — not loud, just present.
- Demon duel tipping (soul buffs landing): layers build — drums and rhythm guitars fade in.
- Demon fall: the drop — full metal.
- The hunt: maximum intensity to the final wipe.

Design rule: intensity comes from LAYER DENSITY, not volume. Adding instruments as the match gets epic, never just turning it up — avoids ear fatigue, critical on phone speakers.
Engine note: Horizon Engine supports FMOD, the industry-standard middleware for adaptive music — the tech for this is native to the platform.
Music is composed/produced in separate loopable stems per layer so the game can crossfade between them by match state.

notes.title: Angel Style (Ultra Instinct-inspired)
notes.body:
Name: open — Sebastian hasn't named this Style. Working reference: the angel Style, inspired by Ultra Instinct Goku.

Fantasy: the body dodges on its own — untouchable calm that flips into raw ranged wrath.

Equipment: bare hands in base form. Ranged attacks in agent form (ranged form not specified).

Attacks: base form fights bare-handed as a tank — no crazy damage. Agent form switches to ranged attacks with raw damage.

Defense: Angel Aura — tap a slot to activate. While active: 80% lower energy consumption; dodge becomes angelic evasion with a 7m maximum dodge distance (evades a 6m ability, cannot evade an 8m ability); cannot regenerate energy while in angel aura. Lasts 3 seconds. 25-second cooldown after deactivation. In agent form defense is low.

Movement: free movement during angel aura. Traversal otherwise not specified.

Abilities: 4-button kit. One button: Angel Aura (tap to activate). 4th button: transform into agent form — requires angel aura to be on and full energy; abilities change on transform. Buttons 1-2: not specified.

Vs demons: not specified.

Not a starter Style — unlockable, harder to obtain. Sebastian's rationale: more complex, more fun, bigger prestige, so a hard unlock path (or premium) fits.

notes.title: Angel Style unlock model
notes.body:
Unlock model for the angel Style, as specified by Sebastian:

- In-game currency is earned depending on match performance.
- Premium currency is purchasable.
- A battle pass (DBZ MOBA-style) contains the Style plus a skin.
- Around 10-15 days after the battle pass ends, the Style becomes purchasable with normal (earned) currency.

Sebastian's position: the premium purchase is pay-to-skip-grind, not pay-to-win.

notes.title: Single sword fighter
notes.body:
Name: open — Sebastian hasn't named this Style. Working reference: single sword fighter.

Fantasy: the honest duelist. Balance between defense and offense. No tricks — the best fundamental tools in the roster.

Equipment: one sword. Fixed kit, no swapping.

Ability 1: swipe in area.

Ability 2: heavy slashes that break guard.

Ability 3: enchantment — the sword gets bigger, hits area damage, all swipes count as heavy. Purges all debuffs on activation (Sebastian chose purge over crowd-control immunity while enchanted).

Might: each damage dealt puts a stack on that enemy, increasing your damage towards them by 5% per stack, 3 stacks max.

Open (proposed, not decided): enchantment tradeoff (slower swings while enchanted); Might stacks decay when disengaging; marked enemy sees the stacks; whether Void shred affects the parry window (recommendation: never — the guard is sacred).

notes.title: Ranged fighter (double pistols + rifle)
notes.body:
Name: open — Sebastian hasn't named this Style. Working reference: ranged fighter.

Fantasy: mark-and-detonate zoner. Stacks the target with pistols, cashes in with the rifle.

Equipment: double pistols and a rifle — one fixed kit, no swapping. Basic attacks are pure pistol.

Passive — funny bomb: each 3 hits puts a stack of funny bomb on the enemy, up to 5 stacks. Stacks can stay on the enemy up to 30 seconds if you haven't hit them.

Slot 1: fires an aggressive amount of bullets with the double pistols, up to 16 hits.

Slot 2: dodge to the back; if an enemy was in front of you, you trap them with an electric field — their defense is lowered by 10% and they are rooted for 1.2 seconds — trapped in place, can still fight (a root, not a stun).

Slot 3: charge the rifle — up to 3 hits on the locked enemy. The rifle gets an 8% final damage bonus for each funny bomb stack the enemy had on; the stacks disappear after the first hit is landed.

Open: whether hitting the enemy refreshes the 30-second stack timer (Sebastian's wording implies it does).
